atpl1:9c31400b90e046d319c28d1317cd1f51.note: FOUNDER/PRODUCT AUTHORED CANDIDATE, NOT CLINICAL REVIEW. Written for the founder/product review of the 3-5y pilot content gap; no clinician has seen it, and reviewer/decided_on are deliberately null. NEW FAMILY: function_question_answering had ZERO candidate and ZERO reviewed content before this card. NO EXISTING CONTENT WAS REUSED — the only curated card in the Parent engine that mentions a function question is `_BUCKET_VARIANTS['expressive_word'][6]` 'Quick Naming Walk', whose success criterion is NAMING objects and whose function question is a make_harder aside; reusing it would have substituted object naming for the function skill, and this family is not in BUCKET_REUSE_APPROVED so the generator would admit none of it anyway. SUCCESS IS SEMANTIC, NOT SYNTACTIC: a one-word answer counts when it gives the use, and no card requires four or more words — sentence length belongs to sentence_building. Mechanism 1 of 7 — REAL OBJECTS, direct question. The most supported form: the referent is in the child's hands and the question is asked about it directly. This is the baseline the other six vary from, and the only card where the object, the question and the answer all sit in the same moment. make_easier names the three NONVERBAL responses that must not count (pointing, demonstrating the use, picking the object up) and says to wait for a spoken answer. Review focus: is a one-word answer such as 'drinking' the right floor for this rung, and is the 'less obvious use' example (a towel, a lid) still familiar enough at 48 months?

SUCCESS IS SEMANTIC, NOT SYNTACTIC: a one-word answer counts when it gives the use, and no card requires four or more words — sentence length belongs to sentence_building. Mechanism 2 of 7 — RECEPTIVE CHOICE AS SCAFFOLD, then the expressive question. Distinct from card 1 because the child first locates the object BY ITS USE and only then says what it is for, so the receptive and expressive halves are separated and can be scaffolded independently. success_criteria states outright that the choice is scaffolding and does not count on its own. EVERY PROTECTION IS UNCHANGED: the item or turn is handed over whether or not the sentence got longer; stop, a break, pain, the toilet, food, water, comfort, safety and help are responded to immediately; one word, a gesture, a sign, a device or a look all remain valid communication; and the legacy line 'Never ignore a clear request to stop in order to get a longer sentence.' is still carried verbatim. Review focus: confirm the low-stakes / essential split is drawn in language a caregiver can apply in the moment.
